title: Exam Technique and Final Review

header.html: exam strategy and review of every domain
the commands in this module were used in the executed labs of Modules 0 to 16 (Kubernetes v1.37.0)

toc.title: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab)

html:
1The time budget

The exam is 2 hours for 15 to 20 tasks. That is an average of 6 to 8 minutes per task, with the passing score at 66%. Points differ per task (the exact points per task are not published on the pages used for this course), so:

Rule Why
Spend the first 2 minutes skimming the whole list if the interface allows; otherwise start in order find the quick wins early
Do easy tasks first, flag hard ones one 15-minute task can cost two easy ones
If you are stuck after about 6 minutes, flag it and move on partial progress on many tasks beats perfection on few
Keep 10 minutes at the end to re-verify a typo in a namespace costs a full task
Do not leave a task half-broken (a half-edited manifest) the checker sees the final state

Where the points are (by domain weight): Environment, Configuration and Security 25%, then Design and Build, Deployment and Services and Networking at 20% each, and Observability and Maintenance 15%. The CKAD has no node or cluster administration: almost every task is a kubectl task in a namespace, and many are quick.

2The routine for every task

  1. Read the whole task, including the last line (names, namespaces, "do not change ...").
  2. Run the context line (kubectl config use-context ...). Check with k config current-context.
  3. Note exact names, namespaces, ports, labels, image tags, file paths. Copy them from the task text, never retype from memory.
  4. Do it with the fastest tool (imperative command, --dry-run=client -o yaml, kubectl explain, one docs page).
  5. Verify with a different command from the one that created it (create with k create, verify with k get -o wide, describe, logs or a test Pod).
  6. Move on.

3Using the documentation well

You may use kubernetes.io/docs and blog, helm.sh/docs, the Quick Reference links in the exam, and distribution documents under /usr/share. You may use the kubernetes.io search; you must not open results from outside the allowed sites.

  • Learn where things are before the exam: Concepts for explanations, Tasks for step-by-step YAML (Pods and containers, probes, ConfigMaps, Secrets, security context, volumes and PV/PVC, Jobs, Ingress), Reference for the kubectl cheat sheet.
  • Prefer kubectl explain for field names (faster than the browser).
  • Copy examples, then change names; do not retype a long YAML.
  • Browser tabs and the terminal share the screen; practice with only the allowed pages.

4Domain checklists

Environment, Configuration and Security (25%): ConfigMap and Secret (create, env/envFrom, volumes, subPath), requests and limits (set resources), ResourceQuota and LimitRange (describe quota), ServiceAccount (serviceAccountName, automountServiceAccountToken), RBAC (create role/rolebinding, auth can-i), securityContext (Pod and container level, capabilities), Pod Security labels, CRDs (explain, api-resources).

Application Design and Build (20%): image (build -t, save, tags), command and args, imagePullPolicy, Job and CronJob (completions, parallelism, --from=cronjob/), DaemonSet/StatefulSet YAML, init containers, sidecars, emptyDir, PV/PVC/StorageClass.

Application Deployment (20%): rolling update (set image, rollout status/history/undo/pause/resume, maxSurge/maxUnavailable), blue/green (Service selector), canary (replica ratio), Helm (repo add, install --set/-f, upgrade, rollback, template, get values), Kustomize (apply -k, overlay fields).

Services and Networking (20%): Services (expose, types, port/targetPort, endpoints), DNS names, Ingress (class, host and path, pathType, TLS Secret), NetworkPolicy (AND versus OR, DNS for egress, deny-all).

Observability and Maintenance (15%): probes (liveness, readiness, startup; httpGet, exec, tcpSocket), API versions (api-resources), get, describe, logs --previous -c, top, exec, debug, events.

5Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab)

Trap Defence
Wrong cluster context run and verify the context line
Wrong namespace (object created in default) -n on every command, or set the context namespace; verify with get -A | grep name
Resource created but misspelled name copy names from the task
Pod fields are immutable delete and recreate (--force --grace-period 0)
Added a container to a running Pod recreate the Pod, or edit the Deployment
Env var from a ConfigMap not updated restart the Pods (rollout restart)
A claim without storageClassName and a PV with manual give both the same class
roleRef immutable delete and recreate the binding
NetworkPolicy blocks DNS allow UDP and TCP 53 in egress
Selector typo = no endpoints get endpoints, --show-labels
latest tag and a local image imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent or a real tag
Probe on the wrong path or port describe pod, test with exec ... wget
Left an answer unverified verify every task
Rebooted base or used the Insert key not allowed

6The final week

  • Redo the break-and-fix labs until you can do each in under 6 minutes: CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError, Pending, probes, Service with no endpoints, Ingress 404.
  • Run the two timed mixed sets (Modules 17 and 18) under exam conditions: 2 hours, only the allowed documentation.
  • Use the killer.sh simulator that comes with the exam registration (2 attempts of 36 hours each, 17 questions per session): it is the closest to the real environment.
  • Practice the speed kit (Module 0) until k, $do and kubectl explain are automatic.
  • Re-read the Quick Reference Cards of every module.
  • Check the current curriculum version and the exam page before booking: the exam moves to a new Kubernetes version a few weeks after each release; rules, fees and allowed resources can change.

7Recall questions

R1How much time per task do you have on average?

Show the answer

About 6 to 8 minutes (2 hours for 15 to 20 tasks).

R2What should you do after about 6 minutes on a stuck task?

Show the answer

Flag it and move on; return at the end.

R3What is the first thing you do in each task?

Show the answer

Run the context line and note exact names and namespaces.

R4Name two fast ways to avoid hand-writing YAML.

Show the answer

--dry-run=client -o yaml and copying examples from the documentation.

R5Which tool beats the browser for field names?

Show the answer

kubectl explain.

R6What is the passing score?

Show the answer

66%.

R7Which domain carries the highest weight?

Show the answer

Application Environment, Configuration and Security, 25%.

R8Which simulator is included with the exam registration?

Show the answer

killer.sh (2 attempts of 36 hours each).

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Time 2 hours, 15 to 20 tasks, about 6 to 8 minutes each, 66% to pass
Order easy first, flag hard, 10 minutes to verify
Every task context line, exact names, verify with a second command
Docs kubernetes.io and helm.sh only
Weights Env 25, Design 20, Deployment 20, Networking 20, Observability 15
Practice break-and-fix labs, timed sets, killer.sh
